title: Property testing and reproducible numerical evidence
outcome: Combine hand-derived cases, generated inputs and invariants so that a plausible but incorrect transformation cannot pass by comparing only to itself.

exercises.title: Derive an oracle
exercises.answer: The hand-derived asymmetric case prevents a uniform-output bug from passing.

exercises.title: Diagnose overflow
exercises.task: Explain why direct sum([1e308,1e308]) is dangerous.
exercises.hint: The desired probabilities are still well-defined.
exercises.answer: Scaling by the maximum gives[1,1], then divides by 2 without overflowing.

exercises.title: Test a permutation
exercises.task: Swap the first and last weights and predict the output.
exercises.expected: The first and last probabilities swap.
exercises.answer: Equivariance checks alignment and catches accidental sorting.

exercises.title: Find a weak property
exercises.task: Explain why sum-to-one alone cannot verify weighting.
exercises.answer: Properties constrain behavior from different directions; one broad invariant is insufficient.

exercises.title: Add an input contract
exercises.task: Specify how negative, all-zero and nonfinite inputs should behave.
exercises.hint: Do not invent a replacement distribution.
exercises.answer: A rejected input gives the caller a chance to correct the model rather than silently changing its meaning.

exercises.title: Transfer to a regression library
exercises.task: Propose properties for predictions from a fitted exact line.
exercises.expected: Known points, shape preservation and permutation alignment.
exercises.answer: Tests should detect coefficient swaps, row reordering and missing intercepts independently of the fitting implementation.
